doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: His son the drummer and Bubbling Brown Sugar
summary: On the Bubbling Brown Sugar European tour, his toddler son took to the drums, played on Guadeloupe TV at five, and became a rock and metal drummer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I guess your son loved it enough to do it, because I see his name. I mean when I googled you I also saw him.

Probably more him than me. He’s a character. Surely more him than me. And then, yeah, see he and his mama, well we had a gig with the show “Bubbling Brown Sugar.” His mama and I. She was a dancer. And I was the lead trumpet player. And we were touring Europe for a year, and he was a year and a half at the time we started the tour. And so, and he was with us all the time. But the first week we were there the music director and the contractor for the show was there rehearsing everybody. We had the week of rehearsal. And, you know, the head music guy was also the godfather of our son. So you know, an old friend. So he saw him looking at the drums and he said, “Let’s put him up on the drums and see what he’ll do.” He thought it was funny, putting the little kid on the drums, right? But instead of banging on the drums he was like, “What will this do, uh huh.” And then they said, “Well wait a minute, that’s not what the kid’s supposed to be doing, he’s actually trying to figure out what they do.” So they let him sit on the drums every day, let him play with the drums. By week’s end he was playing [scats] so everybody got a kick out of it. So the drummer said, “Look, he can practice my drums every day.” And so he would just come and he would practice the drums and we got him © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
a pad so he could practice in the hotel rooms. And that’s just all he would do. And he would watch the show and be playing air drums with his drumsticks.

Oh yes, so that’s all he’s wanted to do. So at five we were living in Guadeloupe and some – he was watching the drummer and some of the singers said, “Well look how he’s just looking at the drummer playing air drums, let’s see what he can do.” And so they thought it was funny but he sat on the drums and was playing. And they said, “Oh man, we have to let him play” and the singer said, “Okay have him play a number.” And it was televised in Guadeloupe so he was five years old and that was his first public gig. And so that’s all he ever wanted to do was play drums.
And he’s doing it full time, is that correct?

Yes, yes. Yeah playing with rock groups. He’s really a jazz drummer. He came up playing all kinds of jazz and he even got to play with Sam Rivers and he got to play with all kinds of people and be around people. He got to play peek-a-boo” with Dizzy Gillespie. But then he got into metal and everything, he’s doing a lot of rock, a lot of metal, and it’s taken him places I haven’t been.
